previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, ICD placement, diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for acute on chronic shortness of breath and chest pressure. The symptoms were likely triggered by noncompliance with his daily Lasix regimen. He was treated with intravenous and oral diuretics, and his lisinopril was safely restarted given stable renal function. A stress test showed no evidence of ischemia but revealed a decline in ejection fraction from 36% to 27%, indicating worsening systolic function. His symptoms improved with treatment, and he was discharged home with home health services. He was counseled on medication adherence, sodium restriction, and smoking cessation, with follow-up arranged with cardiology.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old man with nonischemic cardiomyopathy (LVED ___, 
VT s/p pacer-ICD, AAA s/p repair, DM, chronic renal failure and 
hypertension who presented to the ___ ED with complaints of 
dyspnea and orthopnea

#Acute on chronic exacerbation of congestive heart failure:
Acute on chronic exacerbation of the patient's CHF was thought 
to be the cause of the patient's dyspnea and orthopnea based on 
the patient's physical exam, increased BNP of 4200 and CXR 
revealing possible pulmonary edema. He denied any associated 
symptoms of nausea, chest pain, diaphoresis. The patient had 
negative cardiac enzyme results x2, ECG indicated no changes 
from past ECGs, and thus was ruled out for MI. He reports 
maintaining a good low sodium diet.  In addition, pneumonia did 
not seem likely as the patient did not have cough, fever or 
leukocytosis. The patient was started on 3L O2 by nasal cannula 
to help with respiratory symptoms and responded to 40mg IV 
Lasix.  The patient was given a total of two doses of 
intravenous Lasix and exhibited improved symptoms. 

Despite diuresis, the patient was not able to fully recline in 
bed without being short of breath, but this symptom was much 
improved compared to admission. At the time of discharge, the 
patient had O2 sat of 97% RA and ambulated few times around the 
floor with O2 saturation ranging from 96-98%. Orthostatics 
indicated a BP of 130/___/66 sitting, and 106/70 
when standing. The total I/O over his admission was 120/650. The 
patient's dry weight at discharge was 176 pounds.

The patient had been taken off lisinopril in the outpatient 
setting given concern of kidney function and orthostatic 
hypotension. He was not restarted on the lisinopril as an 
inpatient, as his creatinine was elevated to 1.6 (from baseline 
1.3) on admission and he was exhibiting signs of orthostasis at 
discharge.  He may benefit from re-starting the lisinopril at a 
very low dose as an outpatient for cardioprotection in the 
setting of his congestive heart failure.  It was recommended 
that he follow-up with his PCP and cardiologist in the next two 
weeks.

#History of VT s/p ICD placement: 
During the course of hospitalization the patient was placed on 
telemetry. The patient did exhibit SR/primary heart block during 
many periods. In addition, the patient experienced ___ beats of 
non-sustained VT and VT. The patient's electrolytes were 
followed and no abnormalities were noted. The patient was also 
continued on home dose of amiodarone and Toprol XL. 
.
#Chronic Kidney Disease Stage III:
On admission, the patient was noted to have a Cr of 1.6, which 
was slightly up from the patient's baseline of 1.3. The 
patient's Cr was monitored and at discharge had trended down to 
1.4. As mentioned above, lisinopril was not restarted given 
elevated creatinine and concerns of orthostatic symptoms in the 
outpatient setting.
.
#Diabetes Type II:
The patient's Januvia was held at time of admission, and the 
patient was started on an inpatient Insulin lispro sliding scale 
during the course of hospitalization with the patient's blood 
glucose ranging from 149-212. 
.
#Hypertension:
The patient was continued on home dosage of Toprol XL. 
.
#Dyslipidemia:
The patient was continued on home dosages of Simvastatin and 
Niacin.
.
#FEN: 
The patient was maintained on a diabetic, low sodium healthy 
heart diet with fluid restriction.
.
#Prophylaxis: 
The patient was given SQ Heparin for DVT prophylaxis and 
maintained on a bowel regimen of PRN Senna and Colace.
